data.title: Hiding elements that require JavaScript without JavaScript
data.author: mtlynch
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了如何在不依赖JavaScript的情况下隐藏需要JavaScript功能的元素。作者首先尝试通过在`<html>`元素中添加`js-enabled`类来控制元素显示，但认为这种方法过于繁琐。随后，作者提出了一种更简便的解决方案：使用`<noscript>`标签结合自定义的`d-js-required`类。通过在`<noscript>`内的`<style>`标签中定义`.d-js-required { display: none; }`，可以轻松隐藏需要JavaScript的元素，而无需维护长长的CSS覆盖列表。这种方法简化了代码，并提高了可维护性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何处理网页中JavaScript的启用与否，以及在没有JavaScript的情况下提供适当的用户体验

不同观点：
• [kaszus] 指出CSS媒体查询可以检测JavaScript是否启用，且该功能在大多数主流浏览器的最近两个版本中都得到了支持。
• [theandrewbailey] 建议使用CSS类（如`.d-js-required`）来控制元素的显示，并通过JavaScript动态移除该类以应对JavaScript启用的情况。
• [thefilmore] 提出可以使用HTML的`hidden`属性来处理元素的显示与否。
• [grishka] 提供了一种反向操作的方法，即在`<body>`标签中通过JavaScript添加类，并通过CSS控制元素的显示状态。
• [duncans] 提到了Modernizr JS库，该库可以通过替换HTML类来实现类似的功能。
• [jaredcwhite] 建议将功能封装在自定义元素中，并使用CSS的`:not(:defined)`来隐藏元素，直到JavaScript注册该自定义元素。
• [efortis] 提出另一种方法，即通过JavaScript注入需要JavaScript的元素。
• [giantrobot] 强调了提供JavaScript后备方案的重要性，列举了微浏览器、广告拦截器、糟糕的蜂窝网络和搜索引擎爬虫等多种场景。
• [gjsman-1000] 认为渐进增强（progressive enhancement）已经过时，并引用Hacker News的讨论来支持其观点。
• [winterbloom] 则认为不应该支持没有启用JavaScript的用户，因为绝大多数用户都会启用JavaScript。

补充讨论：
• [bshacklett] 对JavaScript的过度依赖表示不满，并指出一些网站在处理链接时强制使用JavaScript给用户带来的困扰。
• 争议的焦点在于是否应该为没有启用JavaScript的用户提供支持，[gjsman-1000]和[winterbloom]认为不需要，而[giantrobot]和[bshacklett]则认为应该考虑这些用户的需求。
• 不同的技术实现方法展示了开发者在处理JavaScript启用与否问题上的多样化思路，包括CSS媒体查询、JavaScript类操作、HTML属性、自定义元素和JavaScript注入等。

43602688.article_content:
0xdade
Seasonal Influencer. Python dev, security engineer, former red team, former SSD engineer. Hacker, rapper, writer. he/him
4 minutes
Hiding elements that require JavaScript without JavaScript
I’ve tried my best to make sure that this site works great (or at least reasonably well) even without JavaScript, but when JavaScript isn’t available, it can be a little clunky to hide things that do require it. With a mere 7 lines (or a one-liner if you’re nasty), you can easily hide elements that require JavaScript so that you don’t end up with broken functionality visible to users who have JavaScript off.
For context, I’m working on a small share button that I can add to my posts that makes it easy to share my posts however you’d prefer. So here’s an example of what that looks like right now without JavaScript:
While it doesn’t look
hideous
, the link isn’t necessary when JavaScript is enabled, and the SVG isn’t necessary when JavaScript is disabled. I wanted to just show the SVG as a button you can press when JavaScript is enabled, and just show the link to make it easy to copy/paste when JavaScript is disabled.
If you’re not already familiar, the latter part is easy with the
<noscript>
HTML tag. This tag tells browsers to render its contents only when JavaScript is disabled. So making the link only show up when JavaScript is disabled is as easy as wrapping it in a
<noscript>
tag.
But if you want to make an element only appear when JavaScript is enabled, it’s a little less clear cut. There’s not an
<onlyscript>
tag, and the
<script>
tag has a very different meaning than the
<noscript>
tag.
Using JavaScript to indicate JavaScript is enabled
In my first approach with this, I thought maybe I could just add a line of JavaScript in the
<head>
tag that, if JavaScript is enabled, would run and add
js-enabled
to the class list on the
<html>
element.
This would work fine, then I could style things in a special way if JavaScript is enabled, by creating styles like this:
.
share-button
{
display
:
none
;
}
.
js-enabled
.
share-button
{
display
:
block
;
}
But this felt clunky. It results in needing to create two CSS rules for each element, and for my goal of just hiding things when JavaScript isn’t enabled, that seems heavy handed.
This might be a useful solution if you needed to do significantly more elaborate styling only when JavaScript is enabled, but for my purpose, it wasn’t simple enough.
Using noscript to override specific elements
The next solution I came to was to combine the use of the
<noscript>
tag with a
<style>
tag in the head of my site. Then I could just list out elements that I don’t want to show, and mark them explicitly as
display:none;
. They would still be present in the markup, but that’s fine, they shouldn’t get in anybody’s way.
In your site’s header, you can simply link all of your CSS as you normally would, and then add the following snippet to override the fields that you want to not show when JavaScript is disabled. In my example, I was hiding the
.theme-toggle
and the
.menu-trigger
classes. These are related to features that only work if JavaScript is enabled – the three way theme switcher and the hamburger menu dropdown on mobile.
<
noscript
>
<
style
>
.
theme-toggle
{
display
:
none
;
}
.
menu-trigger
{
display
:
none
;
}
</
style
>
</
noscript
>
This is alright. It’s explicit. It relies on existing browser behaviors to do selective style overrides when JavaScript isn’t available, so you don’t have to style both the JS-enabled and JS-disabled cases explicitly. But as I was developing new progressive enhancement features, I didn’t really like this pattern anymore. The more enhanced the website becomes, the longer this list of overrides becomes, and you have to make sure you always keep it up to date if you change class names.
⭐ Using noscript and a d-js-required class.
Since we can append any number of classes to an element, I realized that it makes much more sense to make this noscript-style as simple as possible. We’ll simply create a single class,
d-js-required
to indicate that JavaScript needs to be enabled for us to display this element. We can update our
<noscript><style>
block with just a single class, and then update our existing elements to also use this class.
<
noscript
>
<
style
>
.
d-js-required
{
display
:
none
;
}
</
style
>
</
noscript
>
So now we can have any number of simple elements that only get displayed when JavaScript is enabled, without writing another line of JavaScript, and without needing to maintain an ever-growing list of CSS overrides.
I hope this has given you some inspiration for creative solutions to solve progressive-enhancement problems. If you have JavaScript enabled, you can click the share button below to share this page! And if not, you can just copy the link down below to share this page!

43603091.article_content:
Max severity RCE flaw discovered in widely used Apache Parquet
By
Bill Toulas
April 3, 2025
05:29 PM
0
A maximum severity remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability has been discovered impacting all versions of Apache Parquet up to and including 1.15.0.
The problem stems from the deserialization of untrusted data that could allow attackers with specially crafted Parquet files to gain control of target systems, exfiltrate or modify data, disrupt services, or introduce dangerous payloads such as ransomware.
The vulnerability is tracked under
CVE-2025-30065
and has a CVSS v4 score of 10.0. The flaw was fixed with the release of Apache version 1.15.1.
It should be noted that to exploit this flaw, threat actors must convince someone to import a specially crafted Parquet file.
Severe threat to "big data" environments
Apache Parquet is an open-source, columnar storage format designed for efficient data processing. Unlike row-based formats (like CSV), Parquet stores data by columns, which makes it faster and more space-efficient for analytical workloads.
It is widely adopted across the data engineering and analytics ecosystem, including big data platforms like Hadoop, AWS, Amazon, Google, and Azure cloud services, data lakes, and ETL tools.
Some large companies that use Parquet include Netflix, Uber, Airbnb, and LinkedIn.
The security problem in Parquet was disclosed on April 1, 2025, following a responsible disclosure by its finder, Amazon researcher Keyi Li.
"Schema parsing in the parquet-avro module of Apache Parquet 1.15.0 and previous versions allows bad actors to execute arbitrary code," warned the short
bulletin published on Openwall
.
"Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.15.1, which fixes the issue."
A separate bulletin by Endor Labs highlights the risk of CVE-2025-30065 exploitation more clearly, warning that the flaw can impact any data pipelines and analytics systems that import Parquet files, with the risk being significant for files sourced from external points.
Endor Labs believes the problem was introduced in Parquet version 1.8.0, though older releases might also be impacted. The firm suggests coordinated checks with developers and vendors to determine what Praquet versions are used in production software stacks.
"If an attacker tricks a vulnerable system into reading a specially crafted Parquet file, they could gain remote code execution (RCE) on that system,"
warns Endor Labs
.
However, the security firm avoids over-inflating the risk by including the note, "Despite the frightening potential, it's important to note that the vulnerability can only be exploited if a malicious Parquet file is imported."
That being said, if upgrading to Apache Parquet 1.15.1 immediately is impossible, it is suggested to avoid untrusted Parquet files or carefully validate their safety before processing them. Also, monitoring and logging on systems that handle Parquet processing should be increased.
Although no active exploitation has been discovered yet, the risk is high due to the flaw's severity and the widespread use of Parquet files in big data applications.
Administrators of impacted systems are recommended to upgrade to Parquet version 1.15.1, which addresses CVE-2025-30065, as soon as possible.

data.title: Pitfalls of Safe Rust
data.author: pjmlp
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Rust中的"安全"不仅仅指内存安全，还需处理其他问题以确保程序健壮性。即便在"安全Rust"中，仍有一些编译器无法检测的陷阱，包括类型转换错误、逻辑错误、使用`unwrap`导致的恐慌、第三方库中的不安全代码和竞争条件等。文章提供了多个避免这些问题的建议，如使用检查算术操作防止整数溢出、避免使用`as`进行数值转换、使用有界类型确保数值合法性、确保无效状态无法表示等。此外，文章还强调了在发布模式下启用溢出检查以增强安全性，并提供了具体实现方法。通过遵循这些建议，开发者可以写出更可靠的Rust代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust 编程中的潜在问题和语言特性使用

不同观点：
• **nerdile**：认为文章标题有误导性，"Safe Rust"中的问题并不是特有的，这些问题在其他语言中也存在。建议标题改为"Rust pitfalls: Runtime correctness beyond memory safety"以减少哗众取宠的效果。
• **IshKebab**：对整数溢出和数组越界问题持乐观态度，提到Flux（基于精化类型的工具）可以在不完全依赖正式验证的情况下提供帮助。
• **conaclos**：指出文章未提及替代检查算术的方法，如显式使用Wrapping和Saturating类型，并提到`as`类型转换的替代方案（如`From::from`）虽然更安全但语法较为冗长。
• **zk4x**：认为文章列出的问题很客观，但实际情况更复杂。支持移除`as`转换，但指出某些类型转换（如u64到f32）非常困难。同时，强调性能问题，特别是在高性能计算中需要能够选择退出数学检查，并提到Results和Options带来的分支对性能的影响。
• **bennettnate5**：提到`mem::size_of_val(&T)`的问题，指出其在多重引用类型下返回的结果与预期不符，建议仅使用`size_of::<T>()`。
• **Sharlin**：讨论了`Path::join`在处理绝对路径时的意外行为，认为这是一个潜在的陷阱，并建议可能需要返回`Result`或引入专用方法来处理绝对路径。
• **woah**：质疑`as`是否是一个不必要的陷阱。
• **nurettin**：反对使用`checked_mul`等方法处理溢出问题，认为应该通过编译器标志或静态检测来处理。
• **thrance**：补充提到内存泄漏问题，特别是在使用`Rc`或`Arc`时容易出现引用循环，导致内存无法释放。
• **forrestthewoods**：不认为溢出是一个严重问题，指出Rust已经将溢出行为从“未定义”改为“定义良好的二补码”。
• **quotemstr**：认为文章中关于数组索引的建议是不明智的，数组越界通常表明逻辑错误，应快速失败以防止问题扩大，而不是通过try-things掩盖逻辑错误。
• **sgt**：提出Golang可能在编写健壮软件方面更优，暗示Rust在这方面可能不如Golang。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点包括`as`类型转换的安全性、检查算术（如`checked_mul`）的必要性、以及`Path::join`在处理绝对路径时的行为是否是陷阱。
• 性能和代码简洁性也是讨论的重要方面，特别是在高性能计算场景中，如何平衡安全性和性能成为一个关键问题。
• 不同的开发者对如何处理潜在问题（如溢出、数组越界）有不同的看法，部分开发者倾向于通过工具和编译器支持来解决，而另一些开发者则强调快速失败和逻辑错误检测。

When people say Rust is a “safe language”, they often mean memory safety.
And while memory safety is a great start, it’s far from all it takes to build robust applications.
Memory safety is important but not sufficient for overall reliability.
In this article, I want to show you a few common gotchas in safe Rust that the compiler doesn’t detect and how to avoid them.

You need to address aspects like input validation and making sure that your business logic is correct.

43585742.article_summary: 本文讨论了Rust中的"安全"不仅仅指内存安全，还需处理其他问题以确保程序健壮性。即便在"安全Rust"中，仍有一些编译器无法检测的陷阱，包括类型转换错误、逻辑错误、使用`unwrap`导致的恐慌、第三方库中的不安全代码和竞争条件等。文章提供了多个避免这些问题的建议，如使用检查算术操作防止整数溢出、避免使用`as`进行数值转换、使用有界类型确保数值合法性、确保无效状态无法表示等。此外，文章还强调了在发布模式下启用溢出检查以增强安全性，并提供了具体实现方法。通过遵循这些建议，开发者可以写出更可靠的Rust代码。

主要讨论点：Rust 编程中的潜在问题和语言特性使用

不同观点：
• **nerdile**：认为文章标题有误导性，"Safe Rust"中的问题并不是特有的，这些问题在其他语言中也存在。建议标题改为"Rust pitfalls: Runtime correctness beyond memory safety"以减少哗众取宠的效果。
• **IshKebab**：对整数溢出和数组越界问题持乐观态度，提到Flux（基于精化类型的工具）可以在不完全依赖正式验证的情况下提供帮助。
• **conaclos**：指出文章未提及替代检查算术的方法，如显式使用Wrapping和Saturating类型，并提到`as`类型转换的替代方案（如`From::from`）虽然更安全但语法较为冗长。
• **zk4x**：认为文章列出的问题很客观，但实际情况更复杂。支持移除`as`转换，但指出某些类型转换（如u64到f32）非常困难。同时，强调性能问题，特别是在高性能计算中需要能够选择退出数学检查，并提到Results和Options带来的分支对性能的影响。

data.author: dotcoma
data.article_summary: 欧洲监管机构准备对X（前Twitter）处以超过10亿美元的罚款，因其违反了《数字服务法》。这是该法生效后的首个重大处罚案例。处罚包括罚款及产品整改要求，可能涉及埃隆·马斯克旗下的其他公司如SpaceX的收入。欧盟正在调查X是否在内容审核、广告透明度等方面存在问题，并考虑与其达成和解。X则指责这是政治审查和对言论自由的攻击。欧盟去年12月启动了对X的正式调查，并于2024年7月裁定其违法。

European Union regulators are preparing major penalties against X, including a fine that could exceed $1 billion, according to a
New York Times report
yesterday.
The European Commission
determined last year
that Elon Musk's social network violated the Digital Services Act. Regulators are now in the process of determining what punishment to impose.
"The penalties are set to include a fine and demands for product changes," the NYT report said, attributing the information to "four people with knowledge of the plans." The penalty is expected to be issued this summer and would be the first one under the new EU law.
"European authorities have been weighing how large a fine to issue X as they consider the risks of further antagonizing [President] Trump amid wider trans-Atlantic disputes over trade, tariffs and the war in Ukraine," the NYT report said. "The fine could surpass $1 billion, one person said, as regulators seek to make an example of X to deter other companies from violating the law, the Digital Services Act."
X's global government affairs account criticized European regulators in a
post
last night. "If the reports that the European Commission is considering enforcement actions against X are accurate, it represents an unprecedented act of political censorship and an attack on free speech," X said. "X has gone above and beyond to comply with the EU's Digital Services Act, and we will use every option at our disposal to defend our business, keep our users safe, and protect freedom of speech in Europe."
Penalty math could include Musk’s other firms
The Digital Services Act allows fines of up to 6 percent of a company's total worldwide annual turnover. EU regulators
suggested
last year that they could calculate fines by including revenue from Musk's other companies, including SpaceX. Yesterday's NYT report says this method is still under consideration:
Unlike Google, Meta, Apple and Amazon, which are publicly traded, X is owned solely by Mr. Musk. EU regulators are considering using a piece of the law that lets them calculate a fine based on revenue that also includes other companies Mr. Musk privately controls, like his rocket maker, SpaceX. That increases the potential penalty to well over $1 billion, one person said.
The NYT report said it's possible the EU and X could reach "a settlement if the company agrees to changes that satisfy regulators' concerns." But there is also a separate EU investigation in which regulators "are building a case that X's hands-off approach to policing user-generated content has made it a hub of illegal hate speech, disinformation and other material that is viewed as undercutting democracy across the 27-nation bloc," the report said. This second investigation reportedly could lead to additional penalties.
The EU
announced
a formal investigation into X in December 2023, saying it would "assess whether X may have breached the Digital Services Act (DSA) in areas linked to risk management, content moderation, dark patterns, advertising transparency and data access for researchers." A July 2024
ruling
that X violated the law cited Musk's overhaul of the verification system created when the company was called Twitter, and other changes.
X "designs and operates its interface for the 'verified accounts' with the 'Blue checkmark' in a way that does not correspond to industry practice and deceives users,"
the EU regulator said
at the time. "Since anyone can subscribe to obtain such a 'verified' status, it negatively affects users' ability to make free and informed decisions about the authenticity of the accounts and the content they interact with. There is evidence of motivated malicious actors abusing the 'verified account' to deceive users."
The EU further said that "X does not comply with the required transparency on advertising," and "fails to provide access to its public data to researchers in line with the conditions set out in the DSA."

data.title: Switzerland's vinyl turntable roundabout: Unique road art (2019)
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 瑞士小镇Lyss near Bern附近的一个环岛被设计成一个巨大的黑胶唱片转盘，成为当地独特的道路艺术。该环岛直径12米，唱片部分直径10米，装饰有800个银色金属垫圈。虽然它不会旋转或发出声音，但这个名为KUFA Kreisel的环岛因其创意设计而走红。该设计由靠近环岛的文化场所Kulturfabrik（KUFA）的创意团队完成，历经多年规划，于2019年5月完工。KUFA不仅举办派对，还提供跳蚤市场、 pub quizzes和文化活动。环岛的创意灵感最初包括集装箱和巨型麦克风，最终选择了更符合环岛形状的唱片转盘设计。

Switzerland’s Vinyl Turntable Roundabout: Unique Road Art
Dimitri Burkhard
May 24, 2019
2 min read

Switzerland's flag may be square, but its streets are dotted with roundabouts.
About as ordinary as station clocks, every town has at least one. And since the public is often involved in designing these traffic circles, we have seen horrible things... Think horizontal steel pipes or piles of rock.
But all is not lost, as the town of Lyss near Bern proves. Those who swing by will undoubtedly hit the latest roundabout. And given its decor, does it surprise that the KUFA Kreisel has gone viral?
This roundabout in Switzerland is a giant vinyl turntable.
It doesn’t spin or produce any sounds. Heck, it is missing a tonearm! Even though the traffic circle in Lyss is quite an eye-catcher...
Credits go to the Bern civil engineering department, which had commissioned the roundabout.
The KUFA Kreisel is located at a freeway entrance near a popular cultural venue called
Kulturfabrik
. Its club hosts frequent parties, but the KUFA also offers flea markets, pub quizzes, and cultural events.
It made sense for the creative folks at KUFA to be in charge of designing their roundabout. And after years of planning, the traffic circle was completed in May 2019.
I love the idea of a turntable with a branded vinyl record.
The roundabout has a total diameter of 12 meters, with the record alone being 10 meters. Attached to its side are 800 silver metal washers. According to a person involved, the initial idea was to install a cargo container featuring graffiti art. Another idea was to place an oversized microphone in the center.
From there, the idea of a record player was not too far. But given the roundabout’s circular shape, it made more sense to design a gigantic turntable.
So there you have it: a great reason to swing by the town of Lyss between Biel and Bern. Give this traffic circle a spin before leaving the roundabout for a concert at the KUFA...
While you're at it, check out Switzerland's
record player stamp
or have a look at this
experimental video clip
. providing a new perspective on the roundabout.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国贸易赤字、关税政策及其对经济的影响

不同观点：
• **[throw0101d]、[nipponese]** 引用沃伦·巴菲特的观点，认为关税是一种“经济战争行为”，并且长期来看关税会通过增加商品成本来推动通货膨胀。他们强调了外国对美国资产的过度拥有可能损害美国的主权，并可能带来诸如财富不平等、就业不安全和房地产资产 inflation 等长期问题。
  
• **[tromp]** 提出了一种通过“进口证书（ICs）”机制平衡贸易的方案，认为这种方法可以在不引发贸易战的情况下实现贸易平衡，同时增加出口并促进全球贸易。

• **[BrickFingers]** 表示对长期贸易赤字的影响感到困惑，特别是对普通美国公民的影响。他提到了一系列复杂的经济因素，如预算赤字、美联储利率和通货膨胀，认为这些因素使得贸易赤字的实际影响不明确。

• **[ComputerGuru]** 认为不应该强迫每个国家都实现贸易平衡，比如不能要求柬埔寨必须购买同等价值的美国商品。这一观点强调了全球贸易的复杂性和差异性。

• **[tim333]** 对巴菲特的宏观经济观点持保留态度，认为尽管外国积累美国资产，但实际情况往往并不像巴菲特所说的那样严重。他指出外国持有的美国资产可能通过债务或股权形式存在，而这些可以通过市场力量自行调节。

• **[fbn79]** 反对保护主义，认为关税长期来看会影响公司效率和产品质量。他主张通过消除关税和建立自由贸易区来应对贸易赤字，而不是通过保护主义措施。

• **[legitster]** 指出一个与普遍预期相反的现象，即尽管美国存在贸易赤字，美元却相对其他国家货币升值。他认为这是一种自我修正的问题，如果美元贬值，美国的出口能力会增强。

• **[rayiner]** 提出，除非其他国家从美国购买的商品和服务多于美国从它们购买的，否则美国的贸易赤字将导致外国持有的美国资产不断增加，从而使美国的净资产逐渐外流。

• **[Calwestjobs]** 认为经济战争是持续且全球性的，美国通过全球化进行经济掠夺以维持自身存在。他质疑是否应该改变全球经济模式以追求可持续性，而不是继续剥削其他国家。

补充讨论：
• **[paxys]** 提到巴菲特在2024年大量出售股票和持有现金的操作，与他平时建议的“不要试图预测市场”相矛盾，暗示即使是巴菲特也可能在市场中进行时机操作。

• **[Luc]** 提供了一篇包含模拟和调整巴菲特想法的论文链接，供进一步阅读和研究。

争议焦点：
• 关税和贸易赤字对美国经济的长期影响，特别是对通货膨胀、财富不平等和国家主权的威胁，存在不同看法。部分人如[tim333]和[fbn79]认为市场力量可以自行调节这些问题，而[nipponese]和[throw0101d]则强调其潜在的严重后果。

• **[BrickFingers]** 表示对长期贸易赤字的影响感到困惑，特别是对普通美国公民的影响。他提到了一系列复杂的经济因素，如预算赤字、美联储利率和通货膨胀，认为这些因素使得贸易赤字的实际影响不明确。

• **[ComputerGuru]** 认为不应该强迫每个国家都实现贸易平衡，比如不能要求柬埔寨必须购买同等价值的美国商品。这一观点强调了全球贸易的复杂性和差异性。

• **[tim333]** 对巴菲特的宏观经济观点持保留态度，认为尽管外国积累美国资产，但实际情况往往并不像巴菲特所说的那样严重。他指出外国持有的美国资产可能通过债务或股权形式存在，而这些可以通过市场力量自行调节。

• **[fbn79]** 反对保护主义，认为关税长期来看会影响公司效率和产品质量。他主张通过消除关税和建立自由贸易区来应对贸易赤字，而不是通过保护主义措施。

• **[legitster]** 指出一个与普遍预期相反的现象，即尽管美国存在贸易赤字，美元却相对其他国家货币升值。他认为这是一种自我修正的问题，如果美元贬值，美国的出口能力会增强。

• **[rayiner]** 提出，除非其他国家从美国购买的商品和服务多于美国从它们购买的，否则美国的贸易赤字将导致外国持有的美国资产不断增加，从而使美国的净资产逐渐外流。

• **[Calwestjobs]** 认为经济战争是持续且全球性的，美国通过全球化进行经济掠夺以维持自身存在。他质疑是否应该改变全球经济模式以追求可持续性，而不是继续剥削其他国家。

补充讨论：
• **[paxys]** 提到巴菲特在2024年大量出售股票和持有现金的操作，与他平时建议的“不要试图预测市场”相矛盾，暗示即使是巴菲特也可能在市场中进行时机操作。

• **[Luc]** 提供了一篇包含模拟和调整巴菲特想法的论文链接，供进一步阅读和研究。

争议焦点：
• 关税和贸易赤字对美国经济的长期影响，特别是对通货膨胀、财富不平等和国家主权的威胁，存在不同看法。部分人如[tim333]和[fbn79]认为市场力量可以自行调节这些问题，而[nipponese]和[throw0101d]则强调其潜在的严重后果。

data.title: Charging electric vehicles 5x faster in subfreezing temps
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 美国密歇根大学工程师开发了一种改进的电动车电池制造工艺，能够在寒冷天气下实现高效快速充电，解决了许多潜在买家对电动车在低温下充电效率低、续航不足的担忧。该方法通过在电极上增加微米级通道和纳米级玻璃涂层，防止锂离子电池在低温下形成阻碍性能的锂镀层，从而使电池在-10°C下充电速度提高500%。这种技术不仅加快了充电速度，还保持了电池的能量密度，在快速充电100次后仍能保持97%的容量。该方法有望在现有工厂无需大规模改造的情况下被采用，解决了快速充电、低温性能和长续航之间的矛盾。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：锂离子电池快速充电技术的可行性、应用场景及成本分析

不同观点：
• [Animats] 认为该技术宣称的10分钟快充是在对现有电池生产流程进行较小改动的情况下实现的，尽管目前还没有实际产品。他指出低温性能良好的电池有许多专业用途，例如带有小型太阳能板且没有电网连接的设备，甚至手电筒都可以受益。

• [throwaway41029] 提到了比亚迪在EV快充方面的最新进展，他们宣布的新型超级充电器能够在几分钟内为汽车提供400公里的续航，这对比特斯拉造成了一定影响。他认为这是目前量产技术的先进水平。

• [hinkley] 质疑这种解决方案的成本，并提出使用“加热器”来快速提高电池温度是否更为经济。他认为如果充电速率因温度和化学性质受到限制，可以将多余的能量用于加热电池。

• [ellisv] 提供了相关研究文章的链接，供进一步阅读和参考。

• [wolfi1] 对该技术表示怀疑，认为无法违背Arrhenius Law，特别是在电化学中。他指出离子迁移率在低温下会非常低，除非电池内部温度保持在0°C以上。

• [RKFADU_UOFCCLEL] 赞赏该技术对电池制造商的改动要求极小，认为这是该技术的一个重要优势，因为许多好想法往往忽略了供应链中的其他因素。

• [saurabhshahh] 则关心该技术能否首先应用于智能手机，且不会使手机过热。

• [ajross] 认为尽管该技术可能有优势，但忽略了一个显而易见的解决方案，即直接加热电池。他指出许多早期EV和当今大多数非特斯拉汽车都没有配备电池热管理系统，但它们也不会采用新的电池化学技术。他认为这项技术需要在成本上胜过简单的加热方案才能真正成功。

• [byyoung3] 以幽默的方式提到技术实现过程中可能遇到的极端问题，如在电池着火情况下的充电问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该技术的实际可行性和成本效益，特别是在与其他解决方案（如加热电池）的比较中，其竞争优势是否足够显著。
• 讨论还涉及该技术在不同应用场景（如EV、太阳能设备、智能手机）中的潜在用途和挑战。
• 链接提供的相关研究文章为深入了解该技术提供了更多科学依据。

Charging electric vehicles 5x faster in subfreezing temps
Published On:
April 1, 2025
Contact:
Jim Lynch
Social Media:
Share on:
Share on Twitter
Share on Facebook
Share on LinkedIn
A stabilizing coating on an electrode, combined with microscale channels, helps solve the trade-off between range and charging speed, even in cold temperatures
Engineering student Chloe Acosta plugs in an EV for charging in snowy weather on the University of Michigan’s North Campus. EV charging becomes less efficient in colder weather, but a new strategy for manufacturing battery electrodes could enable charging in 10 minutes in temperatures as cold as -10C. Image credit: Marcin Szczepanski, Michigan Engineering
Study:
Enabling 6C fast charging of Li-ion batteries at sub-zero temperature via interface engineering and 3D architectures
(DOI: 10.1016/j.joule.2025.101881)
A modified manufacturing process for electric vehicle batteries, developed by University of Michigan engineers, could enable high ranges and fast charging in cold weather, solving problems that are turning potential EV buyers away.
“We envision this approach as something that EV battery manufacturers could adopt without major changes to existing factories,” said
Neil Dasgupta
, U-M associate professor of mechanical engineering and materials science and engineering, and corresponding author of the study published in Joule.
Neil Dasgupta
“For the first time, we’ve shown a pathway to simultaneously achieve extreme fast charging at low temperatures, without sacrificing the energy density of the lithium-ion battery.”
Lithium-ion EV batteries made this way can charge 500% faster at temperatures as low as 14 F (-10 C). The structure and coating demonstrated by the team prevented the formation of performance-hindering lithium plating on the battery’s electrodes. As a result, batteries with these modifications keep 97% of their capacity even after being fast-charged 100 times at very cold temperatures.
Current EV batteries store and release power through the movement of lithium ions back and forth between electrodes via a liquid electrolyte. In cold temperatures, this movement of the ions slows, reducing both battery power as well as the charging rate.
To extend range, automakers have increased the thickness of the electrodes they use in battery cells. While that has allowed them to promise longer drives between charges, it makes some of the lithium hard to access, resulting in slower charging and less power for a given battery weight.
Previously, Dasgupta’s team improved battery charging capability by
creating pathways—roughly 40 microns in size—in the anode
, the electrode that receives lithium ions during charging. Drilling through the graphite by blasting it with lasers enabled the lithium ions to find places to lodge faster, even deep within the electrode, ensuring more uniform charging.
This sped up room-temperature charging significantly, but cold charging was still inefficient. The team identified the problem: the chemical layer that forms on the surface of the electrode from reacting with the electrolyte. Dasgupta compares this behavior to butter: you can get a knife through it whether it’s warm or cold, but it’s a lot harder when it’s cold. If you try to fast charge through that layer, lithium metal will build up on the anode like a traffic jam.
“That plating prevents the entire electrode from being charged, once again reducing the battery’s energy capacity,” Manoj Jangid, U-M senior research fellow in mechanical engineering, and co-author of the study.
The team needed to prevent that surface layer from forming. They did this by coating the battery with a glassy material made of lithium borate-carbonate, approximately 20 nanometers thick. The addition of this coating sped up cold charging significantly, and when combined with the channels, the team’s test cells were 500% faster to charge in subfreezing temperatures.
“By the synergy between the 3-D architectures and artificial interface, this work can simultaneously address the trilemma of fast charging at low temperature for long-range driving,” said Tae Cho, a recent Ph.D. graduate in mechanical engineering and first author of the study.
In the past two decades, EVs have become more commonplace on roadways as consumers look for better environmental options, but
AAA survey results
showed that the momentum is hard to maintain. From 2023 to 2024, the number of U.S. adults who would be “likely” or “very likely” to buy a new or used EV dropped from 23% to 18%.

data.title: The Treachery of Image Files (2020)
data.author: appleorchard46
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一系列精致的数字微型艺术作品，每幅作品都是10x10像素的蓝色图像，但拥有独特的“质感”。文章详细描述了每件作品的创作过程和技术细节，包括使用的软件工具和文件格式。例如，一件作品使用Macintosh操作系统和Preview应用创建，另一件则通过Sublime Text编辑PPM文件并用ImageMagick转换为GIF。还有作品通过Vim编辑PPM文件并用FFmpeg生成GIF，以及使用Persistence of Vision Raytracer进行光线追踪生成PNG文件。文章还提到了一件通过Macintosh操作系统 assembler 工具创建的GIF作品，并附带无用的头文件需要修剪。这些作品展示了艺术家在技术限制下的创意表达。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于新闻文章内容及科技公司应对信息泄露的措施的讨论

不同观点：
• 一部分评论者认为科技公司（如Facebook）在应对信息泄露事件时，通常采取公关手段，通过发布声明和承诺改进措施来平息事件，但实际上这些措施往往缺乏实质性改变。他们认为，公司只是在做表面文章，实际保护用户数据的行动有限。例如，有评论指出，Facebook过去多次发生数据泄露事件，但从未真正解决根本问题。

• 另一部分评论者则认为，虽然科技公司在应对信息泄露上可能存在不足，但用户自身也应承担一定责任。他们认为，用户在使用免费服务时，应该意识到个人数据可能被用作商业模式的一部分，因此应对自己的数据隐私保持警惕。这些评论者强调，用户应该更谨慎地选择服务，并利用现有的隐私保护工具，如双重验证和密码管理器等。

• 还有评论者讨论了监管的作用，认为单靠公司自律或用户自我保护并不足够，政府应加强数据隐私保护的法律框架。他们指出，欧洲的GDPR是一个好的开始，但在其他地区，类似的法律仍然缺乏或执行不力。他们呼吁建立全球性的隐私保护标准，并对违规企业施以更严厉的惩罚。

• 有些评论者提到了技术解决方案，如端到端加密和去中心化技术（如区块链），认为这些技术可以在一定程度上缓解信息泄露问题。然而，也有评论者反驳说，这些技术在实际应用中面临很多挑战，如性能问题和用户体验不佳，且并不能完全杜绝信息泄露。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论者讨论了信息泄露事件对社会信任的影响，认为这些事件会逐渐削弱用户对科技公司的信任，最终可能导致用户流失或转向更注重隐私的替代服务。

• 争议的焦点在于科技公司是否真正有能力并愿意保护用户数据，以及在保护用户隐私方面，责任应该如何分配——是公司、用户还是监管机构的责任更大。

• 有评论者指出，媒体在报道信息泄露事件时，往往倾向于夸大其词或选择性报道，以吸引眼球，这也会影响公众对事件的认知和反应。

43604015.article_content:
The Treachery of Image Files
I have recently come into possession of a series of exquisite miniatures which I pray are worthy of your esteemed attention. While my employers are familiar with your
unusual tastes
, they also appreciate your desire for privacy- this showing was arranged with the utmost discretion, I assure you.
To the untrained eye, the pieces might
appear
remarkably similar. Each canvas is a digitally-reproduced composition measuring ten pixels in height and ten pixels in width, illuminated in a strikingly intense blue.
To an, ahem,
avid collector

43604015.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一系列精致的数字微型艺术作品，每幅作品都是10x10像素的蓝色图像，但拥有独特的“质感”。文章详细描述了每件作品的创作过程和技术细节，包括使用的软件工具和文件格式。例如，一件作品使用Macintosh操作系统和Preview应用创建，另一件则通过Sublime Text编辑PPM文件并用ImageMagick转换为GIF。还有作品通过Vim编辑PPM文件并用FFmpeg生成GIF，以及使用Persistence of Vision Raytracer进行光线追踪生成PNG文件。文章还提到了一件通过Macintosh操作系统 assembler 工具创建的GIF作品，并附带无用的头文件需要修剪。这些作品展示了艺术家在技术限制下的创意表达。
43604015.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于新闻文章内容及科技公司应对信息泄露的措施的讨论

不同观点：
• 一部分评论者认为科技公司（如Facebook）在应对信息泄露事件时，通常采取公关手段，通过发布声明和承诺改进措施来平息事件，但实际上这些措施往往缺乏实质性改变。他们认为，公司只是在做表面文章，实际保护用户数据的行动有限。例如，有评论指出，Facebook过去多次发生数据泄露事件，但从未真正解决根本问题。

• 另一部分评论者则认为，虽然科技公司在应对信息泄露上可能存在不足，但用户自身也应承担一定责任。他们认为，用户在使用免费服务时，应该意识到个人数据可能被用作商业模式的一部分，因此应对自己的数据隐私保持警惕。这些评论者强调，用户应该更谨慎地选择服务，并利用现有的隐私保护工具，如双重验证和密码管理器等。

• 还有评论者讨论了监管的作用，认为单靠公司自律或用户自我保护并不足够，政府应加强数据隐私保护的法律框架。他们指出，欧洲的GDPR是一个好的开始，但在其他地区，类似的法律仍然缺乏或执行不力。他们呼吁建立全球性的隐私保护标准，并对违规企业施以更严厉的惩罚。

• 有些评论者提到了技术解决方案，如端到端加密和去中心化技术（如区块链），认为这些技术可以在一定程度上缓解信息泄露问题。然而，也有评论者反驳说，这些技术在实际应用中面临很多挑战，如性能问题和用户体验不佳，且并不能完全杜绝信息泄露。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论者讨论了信息泄露事件对社会信任的影响，认为这些事件会逐渐削弱用户对科技公司的信任，最终可能导致用户流失或转向更注重隐私的替代服务。

• 争议的焦点在于科技公司是否真正有能力并愿意保护用户数据，以及在保护用户隐私方面，责任应该如何分配——是公司、用户还是监管机构的责任更大。

• 有评论者指出，媒体在报道信息泄露事件时，往往倾向于夸大其词或选择性报道，以吸引眼球，这也会影响公众对事件的认知和反应。

data.title: Gmail E2E is as terrible as expected
data.author: HypnoticOcelot
data.article_summary: Google宣布为Gmail引入端到端加密，但其实现方式引发不满。发送者使用自己的密钥加密邮件，接收者会收到一个链接，必须通过所谓的“简化版Gmail”来读取邮件，即使接收者从未使用过Google账户。这意味着，要读取来自Gmail的加密邮件，必须使用Gmail服务，导致浏览器、JavaScript、跟踪等问题。此外，Google允许IT团队强制外部接收者使用受限版Gmail，以控制数据访问和安全策略，这实际上让Google成为邮件的实际控制者。对拒绝使用Gmail的接收者而言，这类邮件无法读取、搜索或管理，只能被视为垃圾邮件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过电子邮件发送保密信息的各种安全方法及其存在的问题

不同观点：
• Freak_NL 认为，由于邮件安全过于复杂，许多服务选择建立自己的安全门户，而不是直接保护邮件。这种做法导致邮箱变成了通知收件箱，且这种局面难以改变，因为相关方不愿放弃这种盈利模式。
• jurschreuder 提到在中国遇到的问题，Gmail中的链接被替换为Google的跟踪链接，导致被防火墙阻止。这种替换链接的做法被认为是不透明的。
• kardianos 指出HIPAA“安全邮件”通常通过发送通知链接来实现，因为这样可以撤销邮件访问权限，并认为标准化和简化这种“消息指针”是未来的机会。
• p2detar 认为端到端加密（E2E）问题早已通过Thunderbird和GPG等工具解决，但云服务的兴起摧毁了这些方案，并质疑这种转变的价值。
• stwrzn 担心如果Google账户或Google本身停止服务，通过其发送的链接和信息将无法访问，不希望这种做法变得更普遍。
• solardev 认为普通用户不会采用PGP，银行和HIPAA“安全邮件”解决方案也采用类似的通知链接方法来确保安全。
• jonathantf2 说明M365的解决方案也是类似，如果收件人在使用MSN或EXO则直接解密，否则通过网页处理。
• commandersaki 质疑通过Gmail链接如何实现E2E加密，认为秘密信息可能在URL中泄露。
• tky 认为减少用户摩擦是推广E2E加密的关键，Google的这种方法在Gmail用户中易于接受，是一个好的开始。
• tptacek 指出这是大多数商业安全邮件产品的标准做法。
• zer0zzz 提到Proton Mail也使用类似方法发送加密邮件，但认为应该采用PGP。
• ranger_danger 担心客户端JavaScript的安全性问题，尤其是在处理E2E加密内容时，认为需要更多的浏览器扩展和验证工具来确保安全。
• fnord77 讽刺地指出，这种方法也可能与广告推送有关。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的争议焦点在于通过通知链接实现安全通信的可靠性和透明度，以及与传统E2E加密方法（如PGP）的比较。
• 有人担心依赖大公司（如Google）的服务会导致未来可能的访问问题和服务中断。
• 对客户端代码的信任问题被提出，尤其是涉及安全内容时，现有的解决方案尚未广泛采用。
• 不同地区（如中国）的网络环境对这类服务的影响也被提及。

43604308.article_content:
Google
announced
that end-to-end encryption would be coming to Gmail.
What a sweet day!
Finally Google does something good.
Is it a new protocol to exchange public keys?
Maybe some way to fetch public key from destination server?
Oh sweet summer child.
The way Big G did it, is in the most annoying way.
The sender encrypts the message with her own key, an email with link is sent to receiver and if he wants to read it, he needs to open something they call "minimal gmail".
Yes, you've got that right.
To read an email sent from Gmail, one needs to use Gmail, even he never had any Google account.
I'm not going into how much this is not E2E, as this has already been proven.
But what I annoyed me the most is how Google assumes that only Gmail is worthy to read email from Gmail.
Until recently, there were basically three subcategories of email:
Normal email
Gmail
Outlook
While the underlying exchange protocol is standardized,the later two have enough big market share to add custom behavior.
And no one cared, because if you're using G or O, you have no one else to blame but yourself (or your employee).
All we care about is being able to send email
to
the big two, which can be pain in the ass (I've heard).
But this power move is different.
If I receive an "e2e" encrypted email from gmail, I will not be able to read it without going to a Google service.
This means browser, javascript, tracking and all that crap.
"IT teams also have the option to require all external recipients (even if they are Gmail users) to use the restricted version of Gmail. This helps ensure that their organizationâs data does not end up stored on third-party servers and devices. It also makes it easier for organizations to protect their data by having the ability to apply security policies and revoke access to emails, no matter how long ago they were sent. Essentially, the E2EE email becomes like a document in Google Drive, allowing the IT team to control its access."
--
Google's documentation
This makes Google the actual owner of the sent message.
I can not read it (I will not open gmail!), I can not search for the email, I can not do anything.
My Email becomes just a notification channel I pay for.
"The recipient can then use a guest Google Workspace account to securely view and reply to the email" my ass.
Ergo: such emails go directly into spam list.

data.title: Gumroad's Interestingly Timed "Open-Source" Play
data.author: pier25
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了作者对Gumroad宣布开源其应用程序的复杂感受。作者首先提到自己对“口香糖”（gum）一词有强烈反感，因此过去避免使用Gumroad平台。然而，考虑到Gumroad对创作者经济的重要性，以及开放源代码对创作者自托管选项的潜在益处，作者对Gumroad开源表示初步支持并分享了这一消息。

但随着进一步了解，作者发现Gumroad存在一些问题。首先，用户指出Gumroad更改了电子邮件规则，且几乎完全用LLM（语言模型）取代了人工客服，导致支持质量下降。其次，Gumroad的“开源”许可证实际上是“源代码可用”许可证，限制了用户在收入达到一定门槛后的使用权限。这与纯粹的开源有所不同，类似于Directus等平台的策略。

最终，作者对分享开源消息感到些许后悔，认为Gumroad在支持创作者控制权方面存在不足，且领导层问题未得到足够关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gumroad平台及其创始人Sahil Lavingia的相关争议

不同观点：
• **burcs**：认为文章杂乱无章，对作者的观点感到困惑。主要记得作者不喜欢“gum”这个词，并对Gumroad的开放源代码计划表示怀疑，认为文章像是在攻击Sahil。
• **dhosek**：关注Gumroad的替代平台，因为对Doge相关的争议感到不安，考虑选择其他平台来销售书籍。
• **mrcwinn**：作为前设计资产市场CEO，不同意低代码和AI工具能解决棘手问题的观点。认为平台的成功在于流量聚集，而不是工具本身的功能。
• **__mharrison__**：因Gumroad及其它平台的“地毯式拉扯”（rug pull）行为，考虑开发自定义创作者平台。提到曾支付高额费用购买“无限课程”，但后来发现视频上传受限。
• **danpalmer**：从个人经历出发，描述Sahil的创业文化，认为他快速行动但缺乏 integrity（诚信）。批评Sahil追逐潮流，包括加入Doge和所谓的“开放源代码”计划，认为这是为了追赶潮流而非真正为用户利益考虑。

补充讨论：
• **ifyouknewone**：指出Gumroad曾试图推出未完成的MOR系统，质疑其动机，怀疑与Sahil加入Doge及规避监管有关。
• **ipsum2**：提到Sahil在退伍军人事务部的工作，认为支持Gumroad相当于支持Sahil在该部门的参与。
• **timestep**：认为Gumroad帮助人们推出产品是积极的，但对开放源代码计划的具体运作方式存疑。
• **Waterluvian**：对Gumroad的维基百科页面显示“11,894个地点”感到困惑，质疑其真实性。
• **aprilthird2021**：对Sahil与Doge合作及其对退伍军人的影响表示失望，曾经欣赏Sahil的诚实和独特的公司运营方式。
• **Kye**：提到Gumroad在Twitter上的一次争论，质疑其道德标准。
• **agentk9**：从工程角度解释，认为开放源代码可能有助于加速开发和问题解决。

In terms of unexplainable quirks
I have as a human being, the weirdest one is this: Gum freaks me out. I hate the idea of it, to the point where I dislike the word.
It really bothers me, like nails on a chalkboard. I’ve never understood why. And it’s to the point where I’ve kind of checked out of things I might like just because their name references the word. (Apologies to
Stereogum
, I’m sure your music publication is just great, the problem is your name.)
So I’ve never been a
Gumroad
user outside of a couple of random purchases here and there. I just couldn’t get past the name. But nonetheless, I respected the role it played in creating what we call the creator economy.
And I’m also an advocate for the creator economy becoming less platform-driven. Someone recently made the point to me that the recent rise in low-code and AI-based tooling is likely going to separate out the platforms that solve tough problems—the Stripes of the world—from those that simply put a nice interface on a problem. And having access to tools that you operate yourself is a way to get there.
Which is why, when I saw that the company had announced it was open-sourcing its application the other day, I got past my weird linguistic quirk and saw something that could be a big deal. I think we need more creator economy things in the self-hostable category, and putting Gumroad in that category feels like it could be a huge kick in the arm for that space.
So I did what I always do: I posted about it. It saw a little bit of pickup, particularly on Mastodon. I noted a quirk of the company’s open-source license that doesn’t truly make it open-source according to commonly accepted definitions, but I otherwise just passively shared it.
But with a little retrospect and a little more digging, I’m feeling less excited about it. In fact, I’m slightly frustrated with myself that I shared it so passively. There are some real problems with Gumroad that make it a terrible foundation for a creator economy that puts the creator in control. And there’s also a big issue with its leadership that almost went unnoticed on the very same day that the news was announced.
So, now, rather than just sharing it, I’m writing about it.

.
TLDR covers the most interesting tech, science, and coding news in just 5 minutes.

Gumroad goes open source! But wait, about that …
Why people are frustrated with Gumroad
First, some existing users have pointed out some issues with the Gumroad service that have made it significantly less useful for the average user. Fellow traveler Evan Hildreth
pointed out two specific issues
: First, the platform changed its rules for when you could email end users, which was annoying but understandable, and more troublingly, the company seems to have replaced its customer support with LLMs almost entirely. As he wrote:
Finally, I asked how to contact Gumroad support. It pointed me to the help site
that didn’t exist
and the contact form within. I eventually found an email on another page and sent a message there; the response was very obviously from the same chatbot.
Chatbots are fine as
one of many
options to access support information. But as the
only
option? When it’s been trained on a help site that references itself (and therefore references a site that doesn’t exist)?
Additionally, the open-source licensing thing is kind of a fib—
it’s more of a source-available license
that limits your ability to use the tool after you hit a certain threshold. It’s not unheard of for this kind of license to be used by companies looking to lean into self-hosting without losing their money train. I have suggested that it can provide a middle ground for folks getting started as long as they’re aware of its limitations.
FOSS die-hards may not agree, but this kind of threading-the-needle can be done well, and honestly, IMHO. A good example is the content-management framework
Directus
,
which essentially makes it free to use
in most cases, unless you make more than $5 million in finances per year, at which point you need to start paying for it. Not purely open source, but it throws FOSS folks a bone by making it so that versions of the software that are more than three years old revert to the General Public License.
How does Gumroad do it?
Well
…
You may use the software under this license only if (1) your company has less than 1 million USD (2024) total revenue in the prior tax year, and less than 10 million USD (2024) GMV (Gross Merchandise Value), or (2) you are a non-profit organization or government entity. 本文讨论了作者对Gumroad宣布开源其应用程序的复杂感受。作者首先提到自己对“口香糖”（gum）一词有强烈反感，因此过去避免使用Gumroad平台。然而，考虑到Gumroad对创作者经济的重要性，以及开放源代码对创作者自托管选项的潜在益处，作者对Gumroad开源表示初步支持并分享了这一消息。

data.author: bryanrasmussen

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：地图制作理论的历史发展及其现代相关性

不同观点：
• **oersted的观点**：地图制作在20世纪中期之前更像是一门工程学科，而非艺术。他指出，准确的航海图和陆地地图在历史上对航海、军事和国家财政至关重要，并且制作和使用这些地图需要高度技术性和资金支持。他不认为地图制作当时是一门明确的科学，但强调了其严肃的工程性质，并认为忽视这一历史对地图制作理论的讨论是不妥的。

• **superfist的观点**：部分理论 cartography 展示了“信息理论潮流”的现象。他引用了Christopher Board的文章，指出到1970年代中期，地图交流模型的历史变得难以管理，因为这些模型变得非常流行，作者们互相借鉴想法，导致科学术语泛滥，尤其是从电气工程等其他领域借用的术语。

• **gryn的观点**：对2001年的文章标题表示质疑，认为文章内容并无新意，提及的工具如QGIS、FME、D3、OpenLayers、Mapbox等在现代工作场所中已经非常普遍，没有提供新的见解。

• **chippadoodle的观点**：对2001年的文章表示质疑，认为自那时以来，GIS和可视化领域已经有了丰富的发展。他还提到Wild Bill Bunge的作品，暗示这些更具创新性和研究价值。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及对历史地图制作的工程性质及其技术要求的认可，同时也提到了现代GIS工具的普及和对历史文章相关性的质疑。
• 争议的焦点在于地图制作历史分类的准确性及其在现代背景下的讨论价值，以及对2001年文章内容的新颖性和实用性的质疑。
• 提到了理论 cartography 中跨学科术语的借用现象，以及在现代技术背景下对历史学术贡献的重新评估。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：联邦支出削减的影响及相关问题

不同观点：
• [rcpt] 认为此次削减开支是意识形态上的清理，而非为了提高效率。支出削减幅度仅为联邦预算的一小部分，但其影响可能超出数字表面。

• [swalling] 指出公共步道维护的联邦支出本就很少，这些削减将使依赖志愿者的步道维护工作更加困难。尤其是灾后重建工作可能无法及时完成，除非志愿者填补更多空缺。

• [almog] 强调削减不仅影响步道使用者（包括徒步旅行者、消防员、猎人），还可能对国家公园和森林造成损害。他们不得不寻找替代路线，而这可能导致更多破坏。此外，提到亚利桑那步道南部终点因未完工的墙而受损。

• [johnnyanmac] 提出政府工会有能力发起罢工，即使非法，但在工作被随意削减的情况下，工人可能没有什么可失去的。

• [throw0101d] 关注内政部长对新鲜烘焙饼干的偏好，质疑其在部门预算削减背景下对个人喜好的关注，并提供了部长的财富背景信息，暗示其可能与普通员工的关注点脱节。

• [outside1234] 预测未来四年将发现被削减的联邦雇员实际工作的价值，暗示削减可能带来长期负面影响。

• [IronCoder1] 讨论自动化的不可避免性，强调政府应激励公司投资于员工的技能提升，以支持被取代的工人过渡到新的经济现实中。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于削减开支的动机和实际影响。一部分人认为削减是出于意识形态而非效率提升，另一部分人关注具体项目（如步道维护）受影响的程度。

• 对内政部长个人偏好的批评，以及其财富背景的披露，引发了对其是否与普通员工和公众利益脱节的讨论。

• 自动化和工人再培训也是讨论中的一个重要方面，提出了在经济转型中如何平衡效率和工人福利的建议。

data.title: Doge's attack on social security causing 'complete, utter chaos', staff says
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 美国社会保障管理局（SSA）正面临严重混乱，员工称由于办公室关闭、人员削减和服务削减，机构濒临“崩溃”。在埃隆·马斯克旗下的“效率部门”（Doge）主导下，SSA计划裁减7000名员工，并试图在数月内迁移所有数据和重写代码，导致系统频繁崩溃。代理局长Leland Dudek承认Doge在主导决策，而马斯克和特朗普等人声称此举旨在打击欺诈。工会代表指出，裁员将严重影响服务和效率，且有进一步裁员风险。员工抱怨管理层缺乏常识和计划，导致社会保障系统陷入混乱。

Doge’s attack on social security causing ‘complete, utter chaos’, staff says
Understaffed agency sent into ‘death spiral’ as employees warn Musk-led cuts will lead to structural collapse
Michael Sainato
Sun 6 Apr 2025 06.00 EDT
Last modified on Sun 6 Apr 2025 12.53 EDT
Share
Office closures, staffing and service cuts, and policy changes at the
Social Security Administration
(SSA) have caused “complete, utter chaos” and are threatening to send the agency into a “death spiral”, according to workers at the agency.
The SSA operates the largest government program in the US, administering social insurance programs, including retirement, disability and survivor benefits.
An average of almost 69 million Americans per month will receive a social security benefit in 2025, totaling about $1.6tn in benefits paid during the year and accounting for 22% of the federal budget. While expensive and challenged by an ageing population, social security remains
overwhelmingly
popular
with Americans. But the agency has been dubbed a “Ponzi scheme” by
Elon Musk
, the billionaire whose so-called “department of government efficiency” (Doge) is currently slashing its staff and budgets.

“They have these ‘concepts of plans’ that they’re hoping are sticking but in reality, are really hurting American people,” said a longtime SSA employee and military veteran who requested to remain anonymous for fear of retaliation. “No one knows what’s going on. They’re just coming up with ideas at the top of their head.”
The SSA website has
crashed
several times this month. Wired
reported
Doge staff want to migrate all social security data and rewrite code in months, which could cause system collapse and further outages.
The agency plans to eliminate the jobs of 7,000 workers at the agency through voluntary buyouts, resignations or firings, though the union representing SSA employees anticipate even more firings beyond cutting staff to 50,000 workers.
Acting commissioner Leland Dudek has
acknowledged
to staff that Doge are making the decisions at the agency. Musk,
Donald Trump
and others have claimed action is being taken to tackle widespread fraud at the agency.
Dudek was appointed acting commissioner after he
reportedly secretly shared
information with Doge staff. He has
threatened
to shut down the agency in response to a court order barring Doge from accessing the data.
“It’s just been a lot of craziness, a lot of foolishness. Until they get rid of Doge and the person in office right now, and the Republicans actually get a backbone and stand up for something for once in their lives, things are just going to be complete chaos. That’s really the best word to describe SSA right now, just complete, utter chaos,” the worker added. “They couldn’t understand the coding, so everything they said SSA was doing illegally, they weren’t. Why are they cutting 7,000 jobs, asked Couture. “It has never been explained with any degree of clarity how they came up with that figure. What’s being served by that by a loss of 7,000 jobs? Our position is that losing 7,000 people doesn’t do any of those things,” he said.
“I don’t think they’re going to stop at 7,000 people lost. If they lose 10,000 or 12,000, they’re running up their high score. They’re able to brag about it.”
Departments at the agency have been closed and reorganized, with workers forced to take reassignments or risk firings, and all workers have been ordered to return to the office five days a week.

around the US.

• [Alifatisk] 以讽刺的口吻表示目前已经达到了web开发的巅峰，暗示当前技术发展可能已到极限。
• [bnchrch] 认为这种看似“愚蠢”的命名和概念可能是下一个基于意图的页面范式，提到通过大量实验和A/B测试来优化页面，但感觉某些关键部分仍未完善，未来还有待发展。
• [blonky] 联想到由_why the lucky stiff开发的创意项目，暗示这种命名风格和创新精神与早期的Ruby社区文化有关。
• [Stwerner] 作为文章的作者，对讨论表示关注，并愿意回答问题或讨论背后的理念，表现出开放和参与的态度。
• [dunefox] 对使用具有不可靠或欺骗性名称的框架表示质疑，暗示对命名的不信任可能影响技术选择。
• [jollyjerry] 提到Cucumber测试框架，将自然语言作为源代码的概念与现有的测试工具联系起来。
• [siliconc0w] 分享了自己创建的一个实验，尝试让AI编写和读取数据库以构建完整的CRUD应用，指出当前AI模型在速度和可靠性上仍有不足，但看好其长期潜力，认为AI可能成为SaaS应用的前端界面补充。

补充讨论：
• 命名和名称的文化意义：多个评论提到了技术框架名称的趣味性和文化背景，反映出开发者社区对名称的关注和反应。
• 未来技术趋势：特别是[bnchrch]和[siliconc0w]提到了未来AI在web开发中的应用潜力，以及当前技术存在的不足和挑战。

data.title: 'Minecraft Movie' Leaks Online: Full Unfinished Version Shared
data.author: austinallegro
data.article_summary: 《Minecraft电影》未完成版本在正式上映前罕见地遭到泄露，部分画面和截图在社交媒体及文件分享网站上广泛传播，尽管这些画面特效尚未完成。尽管盗版 footage 对大制作电影来说是常见问题，但这种早期版本的泄露较为罕见，引发对安全漏洞的质疑。泄露并未显著影响票房表现，该电影由华纳 Bros. 和传奇娱乐制作，预计首周末票房将超过1.3亿美元，可能打破游戏改编电影的票房记录。电影成本1.5亿美元，讲述四个不适应者穿越到方块世界的冒险故事。官方尚未对泄露事件发表评论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于电影《Minecraft》未完成版本（workprint）和幕后版本的讨论，以及对不同地区搜索引擎 censorship 的看法。

不同观点：
• [mystraline] 认为美国和欧洲的搜索引擎（如Google、Bing）在版权审查方面存在 censorship 问题，导致某些链接和网页被删除或 deindexed。相比之下，俄罗斯的 Yandex 等非美国和非欧洲的搜索引擎在言论自由方面表现得更好，没有对相关内容进行过多审查。他指出，在美国，所谓的“言论自由”是有选择性的，某些内容会被媒体和平台屏蔽。

• [jsheard] 则关注电影幕后制作的透明度，表示希望电影工作室能更多地分享未完成的版本，如包含未完成CGI和不同歌曲的版本。他提到《猩球崛起》电影的4K蓝光版本中包含了“原始剪辑”，展示了摄影机实际拍摄的内容。他认为尽管CGI通常被视为不应公开的“幕后秘密”，但这种透明度是有价值的。

• [IlikeKitties] 分享了一个具体未完成版本的详细信息，并提供了下载链接。该用户强调了该版本为工作打印版，并非最终上映的电影版本，包含未完成的CGI、不同的配乐以及颜色调整。此外，还提到音频已同步，并提供了字幕文件和联系方式，邀请他人贡献素材。

• [haunter] 表示已经存在一个质量不错的“盗录版”（Telesync version），但未完成版本因其“粗糙”而具有独特的乐趣。他将这种观感比作YouTube上被移除音乐的视频，认为这种不完美的版本反而增加了娱乐性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是美国搜索引擎的审查机制以及其对言论自由的影响。mystraline 认为美国在版权保护名义下限制了某些内容的传播，而俄罗斯的搜索引擎则相对宽松。
• 另一个讨论点是电影幕后制作版本的分享是否应该更加公开透明，jsheard 支持这种做法，而实际如 IlikeKitties 和 haunter 则分享了具体的未完成版本资源和体验，显示了观众对这种内容的需求。

Warner Bros.
An unfinished version of “
A Minecraft Movie
” leaked online in advance of the video game adaptation’s big-screen debut. Screenshots and footage from the fantasy adventure were being shared widely on social media platforms this week, and were also available on file sharing sites. The images and scenes have uncompleted visual effects. Most of the footage was quickly taken down by the rights holders.
Although pirated footage is a common problem for major film releases, it’s rare to have a working print leak online in this way, raising questions about how such an early version of the movie was accessed, stolen and then shared.
The leaks didn’t seem to dampen turnout, however. Produced by Warner Bros. and Legendary Entertainment, “A Minecraft Movie” is shaping up to be
one of the year’s biggest hits
. The film, which stars
Jason Momoa
and Jack Black, is on target to debut to more than $130 million, which should reinvigorate the slumping box office. At this pace, “A Minecraft Movie” is rivaling the $146.3 million debut of “The Super Mario Bros. Movie,” which set a record for openings of films based on video games.
“A Minecraft Movie” cost $150 million to produce. The story follows four misfits who are sucked through a portal into a cubic world. Officially released in 2011, “Minecraft” has become one of the most popular video game properties in the world and has spawned several spinoffs, as well as an endless array of merchandise.
Popular on Variety
Spokespeople for Warner Bros. and Legendary did not immediately comment on the leaks.

不同观点：

• [simonw]对Llama 4 Maverick和Scout的摘要生成能力提出批评，认为其输出不如其他模型，如Gemini 2.5 Pro。
• [ilove_banh_mi]分享了一种旨在避免模型输出过于模板化的提示设计，强调模型的多功能性和对用户意图的理解。
• [ksec]对Meta的开放性及其在LLM领域的地位提出质疑，指出其在资源投入与成果产出上的不对等，并提及LeCun在AI领域的影响力减弱。

补充讨论：
• [comex]对Llama 4的10M token上下文窗口的技术实现表示好奇，指出标准Transformer在如此大的上下文下会面临二次方级别的计算开销，并询问可能的架构调整。
• [jsheard]指出某些表述（如“it’s important to”）在OpenAI模型中频繁出现，并认为其他模型可能受其影响。
• [hrpnk]提到Llama 4在Groq平台上的可用性和价格信息，提供了Scout和Maverick的具体费用。
• [mrbonner]表达了对当前AI技术快速发展的兴奋之情，将其与JavaScript框架的兴起作对比。
• [hydroreadsstuff]认为GPU在大规模本地AI应用中的地位将被拥有大容量RAM的SoC取代，指出17B参数的模型在256bit LPDDR5x上可以达到足够性能。

争议焦点：
• Llama 4 Maverick在编码基准测试中的表现不佳，引发了对其在实际编程任务中竞争力的质疑。
• 模型的政治偏见问题仍然是讨论的热点，用户对其在政治和社会话题上的中立性表示怀疑。
• 不同用户对Llama 4系列模型的摘要生成能力和输出质量存在不同评价，特别是与竞争模型（如Gemini 2.5 Pro）的比较。

技术细节：
• 讨论中涉及了MoE架构、模型训练效率、多模态能力、10M token上下文窗口的实现技术等技术细节，反映了用户对模型性能和应用潜力的高度关注。

data.title: montasaurus/result: A simple Rust-like Result type for Python 3
data.author: networked
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为`result`的Python库，灵感来源于Rust的`Result`类型，用于处理可能成功或失败的操作。该库提供了两种结果类型：`Ok`表示成功并包含返回值，`Err`表示失败并包含错误信息。通过类型注解，开发者可以清晰区分成功和失败的情况。库中包含如`is_ok`、`is_err`等函数来检查结果类型，并可以直接访问成功值（`ok_value`）或错误值（`err_value`）。此外，还支持使用Python 3.10的`match`语句进行模式匹配。该库简化了错误处理，避免使用自定义异常，并提供了自动生成的API文档。注意，该库是实验性的，使用时需自行承担风险。

data.title: Jeff Geerling won't connect his dishwasher to your stupid cloud [video]
data.author: nikodunk
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了与YouTube和Google相关的一些信息和功能。内容包括YouTube的版权、隐私政策、安全措施、新功能测试以及NFL Sunday Ticket等服务。同时提到Google LLC在2025年的版权归属。文章还提供了关于新闻、广告、创作者合作、开发者信息以及使用条款的链接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：智能家电的隐私、功能和用户选择问题

不同观点：
• **隐私担忧**：[wildrhythms] 担心智能家电会在未经用户同意的情况下连接到开放网络以进行数据传输。这种行为可能侵犯用户隐私，且用户可能对此毫不知情。

• **功能与选择**：[slavik81] 分享了个人经历，提到在购买 dishwasher 时因为不想要 WiFi 功能而选择了非智能版本（KitchenAid KDFM404KPS1），尽管销售人员认为其选择不可理喻。这表明部分用户对智能家电功能并不感兴趣，更注重实用性和个人隐私。

• **智能功能的必要性**：[FloatArtifact] 提到一些家电（如 GE 烤箱）需要依赖 WiFi 才能使用某些功能（如空气炸锅模式），这暗示智能功能可能成为某些产品的必需品，而非附加选项。

• **经济激励与监管需求**：[api] 认为公司有强大的经济动机去收集用户数据，并通过双重获利（如出售数据）来增加收益。因此，仅靠用户的选择不足以解决隐私问题，必须通过监管来限制企业的行为。

• **智能家电的可靠性**：[paulddraper] 通过讽刺性评论“我不能洗碗因为网络断了”表达了对智能家电过度依赖网络的担忧，暗示智能功能可能降低家电的可靠性。

补充讨论：
• 智能家电的 WiFi 功能对用户体验的影响：部分用户（如 slavik81）认为 WiFi 功能并不必要，甚至可能成为负面因素。
• 智能家电的强制性功能：[FloatArtifact] 提到一些产品（如 GE 烤箱）在没有网络的情况下无法使用特定功能，这引发了对智能功能是否应当成为强制选项的讨论。
• 隐私问题与经济动机的关系：[api] 强调了经济激励在推动公司收集用户数据，而用户对此缺乏足够的控制权或知情权。

争议焦点：智能家电的 WiFi 功能是否应该成为默认配置，以及如何在保护用户隐私和满足功能需求之间取得平衡。

• **功能与选择**：[slavik81] 分享了个人经历，提到在购买 dishwasher 时因为不想要 WiFi 功能而选择了非智能版本（KitchenAid KDFM404KPS1），尽管销售人员认为其选择不可理喻。这表明部分用户对智能家电功能并不感兴趣，更注重实用性和个人隐私。

• **智能功能的必要性**：[FloatArtifact] 提到一些家电（如 GE 烤箱）需要依赖 WiFi 才能使用某些功能（如空气炸锅模式），这暗示智能功能可能成为某些产品的必需品，而非附加选项。

• **经济激励与监管需求**：[api] 认为公司有强大的经济动机去收集用户数据，并通过双重获利（如出售数据）来增加收益。因此，仅靠用户的选择不足以解决隐私问题，必须通过监管来限制企业的行为。

• **智能家电的可靠性**：[paulddraper] 通过讽刺性评论“我不能洗碗因为网络断了”表达了对智能家电过度依赖网络的担忧，暗示智能功能可能降低家电的可靠性。

补充讨论：
• 智能家电的 WiFi 功能对用户体验的影响：部分用户（如 slavik81）认为 WiFi 功能并不必要，甚至可能成为负面因素。
• 智能家电的强制性功能：[FloatArtifact] 提到一些产品（如 GE 烤箱）在没有网络的情况下无法使用特定功能，这引发了对智能功能是否应当成为强制选项的讨论。
• 隐私问题与经济动机的关系：[api] 强调了经济激励在推动公司收集用户数据，而用户对此缺乏足够的控制权或知情权。

争议焦点：智能家电的 WiFi 功能是否应该成为默认配置，以及如何在保护用户隐私和满足功能需求之间取得平衡。

About nine months ago, I and three friends decided that AI had gotten good enough to monitor large codebases autonomously for security problems. We started a company around this, trying to leverage the latest AI models to create a tool that could replace at least a good chunk of the value of human pentesters. We have been working on this project since June 2024.
Within the first three months of our company's existence, Claude 3.5 sonnet was released. Just by switching the portions of our service that ran on gpt-4o, our nascent internal benchmark results immediately started to get saturated.
I remember being surprised at the time that our tooling not only seemed to make fewer basic mistakes, but also seemed to
qualitatively
improve in its written vulnerability descriptions and severity estimates. It was as if the models were better at inferring the intent and values behind our prompts, even from incomplete information.
As it happens, there are ~basically no public benchmarks for security research. There are "
cybersecurity
" evals that ask models questions about isolated blocks of code, or "CTF" evals that give a model an explicit challenge description and shell access to a <1kLOC web application. But nothing that gets at
the hard parts of application pentesting for LLMs, which are 1. Navigating a real repository of code too large to put in context, 2. Inferring a target application's security model, and 3. Understanding its implementation deeply enough to learn where that security model is broken.
For these reasons I think the task of vulnerability identification serves as a good litmus test for how well LLMs are generalizing outside of the narrow software engineering domain.
Since 3.5-sonnet, we have been monitoring AI model announcements, and trying pretty much every major new release that claims some sort of improvement. Unexpectedly by me, aside from a minor bump with 3.6 and an even smaller bump with 3.7, literally none of the new models we've tried have made a significant difference on either our internal benchmarks or in our developers' ability to find new bugs. This includes the new test-time OpenAI models.
At first, I was nervous to report this publicly because I thought it might reflect badly on us as a team. Our scanner has improved a lot since August, but because of regular engineering, not model improvements. It could've been a problem with the architecture that we had designed, that we weren't getting more milage as the SWE-Bench scores went up.
But in recent months I've spoken to other YC founders doing AI application startups and most of them have had the same anecdotal experiences: 1. o99-pro-ultra announced, 2. Benchmarks look good, 3. Evaluated performance mediocre. This is despite the fact that we work in different industries, on different problem sets. Sometimes the founder will apply a cope to the narrative ("We just don't have any PhD level questions to ask"), but the narrative is there.
I have read the studies. I have seen the numbers. Maybe LLMs are becoming more fun to talk to, maybe they're performing better on controlled exams. But I would nevertheless like to submit, based off of internal benchmarks, and my own and colleagues' perceptions using these models, that whatever gains these companies are reporting to the public, they are not reflective of economic usefulness or generality. They are not reflective of my Lived Experience or the Lived Experience of my customers. In terms of being able to perform entirely new tasks, or larger proportions of users' intellectual labor, I don't think they have improved much since August.
Depending on your perspective, this is good news! Both
for me personally
, as someone trying to make money leveraging LLM capabilities while they're too stupid to solve the whole problem, and for people worried that a quick transition to an AI-controlled economy would present moral hazards.
At the same time, there's an argument that the disconnect in model scores and the reported experiences of highly attuned consumers is a bad sign. If the industry can't figure out how to measure even the
intellectual ability
of models now, while they are mostly confined to chatrooms, how the hell is it going to develop metrics for assessing the
impact
of AIs when they're doing things like managing companies or developing public policy? If we're running into the traps of Goodharting before we've even delegated the messy hard parts of public life to the machines, I would like to know why.
Are the AI labs just cheating?
AI lab founders believe they are in a civilizational competition for control of the entire future lightcone, and will be made Dictator of the Universe if they succeed. Accusing these founders of engaging in fraud to further these purposes is quite reasonable. Even if you are starting with an

data.title: The Importance of Fact-Checking
data.author: NaOH
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了Ira Glass的《This American Life》广播节目的哲学和故事叙述方式。文章指出，新闻通常缺乏亚里士多德所说的故事核心要素——情节，而Glass通过情节设计吸引听众，解决现代观众注意力短暂和政治文化两极化的问题。文章特别提到2019年11月15日的节目《The Out Crowd》，该节目聚焦特朗普政府的“留在墨西哥”政策对寻求庇护者的影响，并通过讲述九岁洪都拉斯难民Darwin的故事，使听众更关注人性的层面。尽管该节目多次成功，但也有一次重大失误。文章强调，通过角色、场景和意外时刻的叙述，能让观众更深入了解事件，持续关注故事发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：媒体中事实与故事讲述的关系，以及真相在新闻和娱乐中的地位。

不同观点：
• Isamu认为Tucker Carlson的节目不应被视为新闻，而应视为“故事时间”，而Fox的“意见”节目 lineup中的内容常被观众误认为是事实，导致问题。Carlson案的胜诉显示出他在言论中避免明确陈述事实以规避责任。
• gcp123强调媒体中的故事叙述对听众的影响力，以及在追求情感共鸣时可能导致的造假问题。Daisey事件被用作公共广播中的伦理案例，显示出在追求叙事完美时可能忽视真相的危险。
• otterley认为犯错是人之常情，关键在于如何纠正错误。赞赏Ira Glass团队在发现错误后做出的正确反应。
• pards指出Daisey事件的具体细节，特别是在2012年“This American Life”对该事件的“撤稿”处理。
• glenstein批评Daisey的辩解，将其与Hasan Minhaj的“情感真相”相比较，认为这是对客观现实的忽视。
• diggetmaster提出有争议的问题往往有多个事实面， biased的故事通常只呈现一面而忽略另一面，即使经过事实核查也难以发现所有问题。
• kjellsbells引用纽约时报的Caliphate播客系列作为另一个TAL格式失败的例子，显示出即使知名媒体也会因追求叙事而忽略事实。
• blindriver认为现代人更关注“氛围”而非事实，建议从一手资料获取信息，因为即使是“可靠”的媒体也有其议程。
• cle指出媒体常通过暗示因果关系或使用误导性的事实来影响观众，即使100%的事实也可能被用来支持错误的结论。
• croes认为人们更倾向于被故事吸引，而非事实。故事比事实更容易传播，这也是民粹主义成功的原因。
• femiagbabiaka认为媒体造假服务于美国国务院的议题，并指出当前主流媒体在加沙报道中重复同样的模式。
• g42gregory强调自己做事实核查的重要性，建议阅读原始文件和法庭报告，而不是依赖NYT/WSJ/FT等媒体的报道。
• spaceisballer提到《The Lifespan of a Fact》一书，认为该书探讨了事实核查与故事叙述之间的界限问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于媒体如何在追求叙事效果的同时保持事实的真实性，以及观众如何在信息获取中辨别真相。
• 讨论还涉及到现代媒体的可信度问题，以及如何通过教育和事实核查来提高公众对真相的认知。
• 不同评论者对于如何解决这些问题提出了不同的建议，包括加强事实核查、依赖一手资料、以及提高公众媒体素养等。

On the Episode That Changed Ira Glass’s
This American Life
Forever
Or, On the Importance of Fact-Checking
via Avid Reader Press
By
Steve Oney
March 31, 2025
The philosophy that animates Ira Glass’s
This American Life
can be summed up by a simple come on: “Let me tell you a story.” News, almost by definition, rarely conforms to what Aristotle deemed the essential element of storytelling: plot. It consists of dispatches from geographically disparate locales and varying worlds (politics, foreign affairs, finance, sports), and it doesn’t adhere to a scenario.
Article continues after advertisement
Remove Ads
Of late, the proliferation of offerings from online outlets has increased choices while fragmenting audiences, creating an age of hot takes and short attention spans. It’s hard to get consumers of TV and radio news to stay tuned. “Having a plot is a way to make people stick around and provide something that feels satisfying,” Ira Glass noted. “That’s the thing about it that’s helpful. If you have a plot, the story can be mundane. It can be incredibly everyday. But people just want to find out what’s gonna happen, and they’ll hang around.”
Not only this, but plot—or narrative, as its sometimes more grandly called—offers an antidote to the political and cultural polarization changing audience habits. As Glass put it: “The primary problem you have in doing a story about any of the big, emotional issues of our time—was the election stolen, does the vaccine work, what to think of Donald Trump, climate change—is that everybody already knows what they think. If you start any story, everybody’s like, ‘Yeah, yeah, I know.’ There’s an enormous hurdle to get over to get people to listen past even the first thirty-five seconds. What do you do? By having characters, scenes, and surprising moments and just letting the thing unfold, you can catch people up in the lives of the people you’re documenting. And then they’ll keep listening to hear how things work out.”
The apotheosis of the
This American Life
approach is its November 15, 2019, episode, “The Out Crowd,” winner of the inaugural Pulitzer Prize for audio journalism. When the staff of
TAL
began to put together this show, which focuses on how the Trump administration’s Remain in Mexico policy affected asylum seekers trying to cross into the United States, the basic facts of the matter were already familiar. “We knew this had gotten coverage in the
Wall Street Journal
, the
New York Times
, the
Washington Post
, and on the networks,” recalled Glass. “It’s out there—if you follow this. But all of the stories felt academic.” The goal was to capture the human dimensions of a policy that had stranded thousands in desolate shelters deemed unsafe by the US State Department.
“The Out Crowd” opens with a fourteen-minute prologue reported from a tent city in Matamoros, Mexico, just across the Rio Grande from Brownsville, Texas. In it, Glass introduces listeners to an unlikely protagonist—a nine-year-old Honduran refugee named Darwin who along with his mother is hoping to get to America. “I feel like if you said at the beginning that this was a show about immigration, nobody would listen,” said Glass. “The fact that the first few minutes of the show can just be a portrait of this completely charming kid, everybody’s favorite kid—you wanna hear more. Then you pull the camera back. Then you reveal: OK. Here’s what the show is about today.”

43549893.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了Ira Glass的《This American Life》广播节目的哲学和故事叙述方式。文章指出，新闻通常缺乏亚里士多德所说的故事核心要素——情节，而Glass通过情节设计吸引听众，解决现代观众注意力短暂和政治文化两极化的问题。文章特别提到2019年11月15日的节目《The Out Crowd》，该节目聚焦特朗普政府的“留在墨西哥”政策对寻求庇护者的影响，并通过讲述九岁洪都拉斯难民Darwin的故事，使听众更关注人性的层面。尽管该节目多次成功，但也有一次重大失误。文章强调，通过角色、场景和意外时刻的叙述，能让观众更深入了解事件，持续关注故事发展。

data.article_summary: TinyWall是一个免费、轻量、非侵入式的Windows防火墙，采用GPL-3.0许可证。该项目的源代码托管在GitHub上，虽然上游开发已基本停滞，但开发者欢迎社区提交改进或创建分支。构建TinyWall需要使用Microsoft Visual Studio 2019或2022以及Wix v3.14工具集。构建过程包括编译应用程序、更新数据库和制作安装程序。贡献代码需创建功能分支、提交更改并发起拉取请求。若开发新功能，建议先联系项目维护者。使用不同名称的TinyWall分支版本可自行构建和分发。项目主要使用C#编写。

A free, lightweight and non-intrusive firewall

About this repository
This is the source code of TinyWall as found at its
website
. Upstream development is now largely inactive, but this repository is provided for anyone who would like to submit their own improvements or fork the project.
How to build
Necessary tools
Microsoft Visual Studio 2019 or 2022
Wix v3.14 Toolset
Visual Studio extension for Wix v3 Toolset
To build the application
Open the solution file in Visual Studio and compile the
TinyWall
project. The other projects referenced inside the solution need not be compiled separately as they will be statically compiled into the application.
Done.
To update/build build the database of known applications
Adjust the individual JSON files in the
TinyWall\Database
folder.
Start the application with the
/develtool
flag.
Use the
Database creator
tab to create one combined database file in JSON format. The output file will be called
profiles.json
.
To use the new database in debug builds, copy the output file to the
TinyWall\bin\Debug
folder.
Done.
To build the installer
Copy the compiled application files and all dependencies into the
MsiSetup\Sources\ProgramFiles\TinyWall
folder.
Update the files as necessary inside the
MsiSetup\Sources\CommonAppData\TinyWall
folder. See instructions above about creating the database.
Open the solution file in Visual Studio and compile the
MsiSetup
project.
Done.
Contributing
Please don't open issues for feature requests or bug reports. Any changes you'd like you will need to implement yourself. If you have improvements that you would like to integrate into TinyWall, please fork the repo and create a pull request.
Fork the Project
Create your Feature Branch (
git checkout -b feature/AmazingFeature
)
Commit your Changes (
git commit -m 'Add some AmazingFeature'
)
Push to the Branch (
git push origin feature/AmazingFeature
)
Open a Pull Request
For complex features or large changes, please contact me first if your changes are still within the scope of the application.
If you prefer that, you can also build and distribute your own version of the binaries. In this case though you need to choose a different name other than TinyWall for your application.

pylorak.Windows\TaskDialog
) written by KevinGre (

All other code in the repository is under the GNU GPLv3 License. See
LICENSE.txt
for more information.

data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Rauthy是一个轻量级、易用的OpenID Connect身份提供者，注重安全性和灵活性。它使用Rust编写，具有高效的内存和性能表现，可运行于各种硬件上，支持物联网和无界面工具的单点登录（SSO）。Rauthy默认启用高安全选项，如Passkeys和ed25519算法，支持无密码登录和多因素认证（MFA）。它提供高可用性、客户端品牌定制、UI翻译、管理界面、事件审计等功能，默认使用Hiqlite数据库，也可选择Postgres。Rauthy设计注重效率，资源占用低，可在如Raspberry Pi上运行，同时通过缓存机制提升速度。部分配置仅可通过配置文件静态设置。

Rauthy
Rauthy - OpenID Connect Single Sign-On Identity & Access Management
What it is
Rauthy is a lightweight and easy to use OpenID Connect Identity Provider. It aims to be simple to both set up and
operate, with very secure defaults and lots of config options, if you need the flexibility. It puts heavy emphasis on
Passkeys and a very strong security in general. The project is written in Rust to be as memory efficient, secure and
fast as possible, and it can run on basically any hardware. If you need Single Sign-On support for IoT or headless
CLI tools, it's got you covered as well.
You get High-Availability, client branding, UI translation, a nice Admin UI, Events and Auditing, and many more
features. By default, it runs on top of
Hiqlite
and does not depend on an external
database (Postgres as an alternative) to make it even simpler to operate, while scaling up to millions of users easily.
Secure by default
It tries to be as secure as possible by default while still providing all the options needed to be compatible with
older systems. For instance, if you create a new OIDC client, it activates
ed25519
as the default algorithm for
token signing and S256 PKCE flow. This will not work with clients, which do not support it, but you can of course
deactivate this to your liking.
MFA and Passwordless Login
Option 1:
Password + Security Key (without User Verification):
Rauthy provides FIDO 2 / Webauthn login flows. If you once logged in on a new client with your username + password,
you will get an encrypted cookie which will allow you to log in without a password from that moment on. You only need to
have a FIDO compliant Passkey being registered for your account.
Option 2:
Passkey-Only Accounts:
Rauthy supports Passkey-Only-Accounts: you basically just provide your E-Mail address and log in with
your FIDO 2 Passkey. Your account will not even have / need a password. This login flow is restricted though to only
those passkeys, that can provide User Verification (UV) to always have at least 2FA security.
Discoverable credentials are discouraged with Rauthy (for good reason). This means you will need to enter your E-Mail
for the login (which will be autofilled after the first one), but Rauthy passkeys do not use any storage on your
device. For instance when you have a Yubikey which can store 25 passkeys, it will not use a single slot there even
having full support.
Fast and efficient
The main goal was to provide an SSO solution like Keycloak and others while using a way lower footprint and being more
efficient with resources. For instance, Rauthy can easily run a fully blown SSO provider on just a Raspberry Pi. It
makes extensive use of caching for everything used in the authentication chain to be as fast as possible. Most things
are even cached for several hours and special care has been taken into account in case of cache eviction and
invalidation.
Rauthy comes with two database options:
with embedded
Hiqlite
, which is the default setting
or you can optionally use a Postgres as your database, if you already have an instance running anyway.
A deployment with the embedded
Hiqlite
, filled caches / buffers and a small set of
clients and users configured typically settles around 65MB of memory. Using Postgres, it will end up at ~45MB, but then
you have of course your Postgres consuming additional resources. If a password from a login is hashed, the memory
consumption will of course go up way higher than this, depending on your configured Argon2ID parameters.
For achieving the speed and efficiency, some additional design tradeoffs were made. For instance, some things can only
be statically set via config file and not dynamically via UI, because most of them are configured once and then never
touched again.

data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 本文主要讨论了美国国家海洋和大气管理局（NOAA）在特朗普政府下面临的重大变化及其潜在影响。NOAA成立于1970年，其前身可追溯至1807年，负责调查美国海岸、气象和渔业等。目前，NOAA在全球拥有约12,000名员工，负责监测海洋、大气、渔业和海洋生物，并提供天气预报以保护民众和财产。然而，在特朗普政府推行的削减成本措施下，NOAA在2024财年面临严重的人手不足和预算削减，已有880名员工被解雇，尽管部分人员后来被临时恢复职位，但许多人处于行政休假状态。此外，政府还考虑终止NOAA运营场所的租赁，并从联邦机构中删除某些词汇，如“气候科学”。专家担心这些削减将严重影响NOAA的极端天气预报和气候研究能力，可能导致天气预报不准确，危及公众安全，尤其是在春季恶劣天气和即将到来的飓风季节中。

I
n 1807
, President Thomas Jefferson
founded
the nation’s first scientific agency. It was tasked with surveying the coasts of the United States. Roughly 60 years later, a national weather bureau was
created
, and a fish and fisheries commission soon
followed
. The focus of these three agencies was eventually brought together in 1970 as part of the new National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, or NOAA. Today, agency staff study the ocean and atmosphere, share knowledge, and conserve coastal and marine ecosystems. Under the new administration of Donald Trump, this agency with 218-year-old roots is undergoing another significant change — one that experts fear could significantly hamper NOAA’s work.
CROSS SECTIONS:
Dissecting the contentious and the controversial — with science at the core.
In fiscal year 2024, NOAA
accounted for
more than half of the Department of Commerce’s budget and, as of recently, it had about
12,000 employees
worldwide. The agency has a broad portfolio of activities, including gathering data and monitoring oceans, the atmosphere, fisheries, and marine life. The National Weather Service, a NOAA sub-agency, provides weather forecasts that include watches and warnings used to protect people and their property. To carry out its work, NOAA has at its disposal an
array
of tools, including satellites, airplanes, weather balloons, maritime buoys, and radar systems.
Under the direction of the
Department of Government Efficiency
, the administration’s cost-cutting effort, CBS reported that
880
NOAA employees were let go in late February. In March, a U.S. district judge
ordered
thousands of fired federal workers to be temporarily reinstated, but many have been put on
administrative leave
. The administration has also discussed
possibly terminating leases
for properties housing NOAA operations. Moreover, all federal agencies are currently subject to a
purge
of certain words and phrases. The New York Times has found that “climate science” is among them.
“One could make a strong case that NOAA was under-resourced and under-staffed before these cuts, so this is simply making the situation worse,” wrote Keith Seitter, former executive director of the American Meteorological Society, in an email to Undark. This could lead to dangerous
delays
in forecasting extreme weather events like tornadoes and hurricanes, in addition to hampering
climate research
. Private entities aren’t likely to be able to fill the void, Seitter noted.
“There seems little question that these cuts are going to severely impair NOAA’s ability to carry out its mission,” he wrote.
T
rump and his
supporters have long
criticized
NOAA’s climate research efforts as being politically motivated. Project 2025, a sprawling document created by the conservative Heritage Foundation, describes NOAA as a main driver of the “climate change alarm industry,” and suggests the climate research of one of its divisions ought to be “disbanded.” The document further states that some of NOAA’s other functions could be carried out in the private sector “at lower cost and higher quality.” The National Weather Service, for example, could be commercialized, according to Project 2025.
Related
In the War Against DEI in Science, What Is Lost?
Massachusetts-based meteorologist Brian Gonsalves wrote in an email to Undark: “We are already seeing immediate impacts from these cuts, which will only worsen if further cuts are made.” The reduced staffing could make it more difficult to gather and process the data coming in from across the country — on temperature, wind speed, and dew points, among other things. The end result may be a decline in the agency’s ability to produce accurate weather forecasts, he said.
This may ultimately put people’s
safety at risk
. Seitter, currently a visiting professor of environmental studies and geosciences at the College of the Holy Cross, pointed to the arrival of spring’s severe weather season. “It would not be a surprise to see insufficient staffing available to do some of the really important planning and preparation with state and local emergency managers,” he said. data.title: Baby Steps into Genetic Programming
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者使用Common Lisp进行遗传编程（Genetic Programming, GP）的初步探索，目标是通过进化算法找到计算圆面积的公式。文章分为多个部分，从随机代码生成、运行代码、种群进化到适应度评估等。作者首先定义了基本的操作符（+，-，*，/）和随机选择元素的函数`RANDOM-ELT`，接着介绍了生成随机函数表达式的过程，这些表达式由随机操作符和参数构成。随后，文章讨论了如何运行生成的代码、创建种群以及通过交叉和变异进化种群。最后，作者总结了整个过程，并鼓励读者在REPL环境中自行尝试这些代码。文章内容偏重实践，代码示例丰富，理论解释较少，适合对GP或Common Lisp感兴趣的初学者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于遗传编程（Genetic Programming, GP）及其替代方法、适用场景和实际应用的讨论

不同观点：
• abhgh推荐使用贝叶斯优化（Bayesian Optimization, BayesOpt）作为遗传编程的现代替代方案，认为贝叶斯优化具有更坚实的理论基础，并在近年得到了进一步发展。他还提供了相关书籍和教程链接，并指出贝叶斯优化在超参数调优和分子发现等非可微目标函数场景中非常实用。
• mark_l_watson认为abhgh的评论简明扼要，但建议如果对遗传编程感兴趣，最终还是应该阅读John Koza的经典书籍或尝试其实现代码，并提醒不要将遗传算法（GA）与遗传编程（GP）混淆。
• arscan回忆了自己在2011年参加的Google AI竞赛“ants”，认为虽然获胜方案不如预期优雅，但非常有效。
• hintymad提出一个基础问题，即在深度学习流行的当下，遗传编程最适合解决哪些问题，并询问是否存在将遗传编程与深度学习结合的模型。
• artful314w指出ai-contest.com链接指向了一个无关且可疑的网站。
• nickpsecurity分享了自己使用基本编程技术实现遗传算法的经验，包括解决64位全1问题、贷款偿还计划优化等，并提到了一些适合初学者的简单示例。
• user_of_the_wek无关地关心了一个婴儿的安危。
• ggerules对帖子表示赞赏。
• Cogito提醒读者帖子内容来自2011年。
• ribs认为遗传编程在过去并不被看好，对人们在此讨论它感到惊讶，但同时也指出不同方法的效果因具体情况而异（YMMV）。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是遗传编程与贝叶斯优化的相对优势，abhgh更推崇贝叶斯优化，而ribs则对其效果持怀疑态度。
• 另一个讨论点是遗传编程与遗传算法的区别，mark_l_watson特别指出了这一点。
• 实际应用场景的讨论，包括nickpsecurity提到的简单演示示例和abhgh提到的超参数调优和分子发现等。
• 链接和资源分享，如abhgh提供的贝叶斯优化书籍和教程链接，以及nickpsecurity提到的初学者示例链接。

总的来说，讨论围绕遗传编程及其替代方法的适用性和实际应用展开，涉及具体案例、理论对比和实用资源。

1
Introduction
While my final ranking in the Google AI Contest was disappointing
(
280th
), it was a very educational experience and was totally offset
by
Gábor Melis' dominating win
using Common Lisp as well.
One of things that piqued my interest during the contest was
a post on the AI Challenge forums
about a bot written using
genetic programming
.
Genetic programming (GP) and
genetic algorithms
have always held my
interest but
seeing the bot in action
really motivated me to dive into
the matter.
Genetic programming is inspired by biological evolution and is a way
of solving problems by setting up an environment (tuned to the problem
at hand!) and allowing computer programs to evolve towards a possible
solution in that environment.
This article shows my initial exploration into GP using Common Lisp
and should be an example of a typical
REPL
session (my session was a
couple of hours divided over two evenings).  The code has been
reviewed, made a more readable and lispier but still looks very much
like what I wrote initially.  From the REPL session useful output has
been cut and pasted into this article.
This is a
really
basic introduction into GP and is meant for people
interested in GP and/or interested in (Common) Lisp.  It is heavy on
code and examples and light on theory.  My intention is for the reader
to play around with the functions on the REPL as they come by in the
article.
The code in this article should be portable Common Lisp.  If you need
to know what a function or macro does please consult the
Common Lisp HyperSpec
.
1.1
Toy Project
I found
A Field Guide to Genetic Programming
on-line and decided to
duplicate
Bill Clementson's toy project
of discovering the formula for
calculating the area of a circle.  Except for educational purposes we
will be starting from scratch.
1.2
Environment
Many Common Lispers use Emacs,
Slime
and usually Unix or OS X as
development environment.  However, do not get the impression this is
the only way to write Lisp.  The
development page on CLiki
lists many
other alternatives in various states of usability.
My recommendation is to use your favorite text editor and
CLISP
since
it comes with command line history and tab completion built in.  Write
or paste the code in your editor and save the file after every
addition as for example "
gp.lisp
".  Then you only need to type:
(load "/path/to/gp.lisp")
once and can use the command line history to reload it.
2
Generating Random Code
As you might have read, the
space.invaders
bot was written in PHP.
Our weapon of choice is Common Lisp and the first matter of business
is generating random code.
2.1
Operators
(
defparameter
*operators*
'(+ - * /))
To keep things simple and already knowing our target function (πr²) we
opt for using four operators: addition, subtraction, multiplication
and division.  In the name of simplicity (again) they will have an
arity of 2, so they will all take two arguments.
*OPERATORS* is the name of the  variable.  The *earmuffs* convention
is used to signify global variables.
2.2
RANDOM-ELT
(
defun
random-elt
(sequence)
(
let
((seq-length (length sequence)))
(
when
(> seq-length 0)
(elt sequence (random seq-length)))))
The function RANDOM-FORM in the next section uses RANDOM-ELT to select
a random element from the list of operators.
2.3
Generating Random
Function Forms
(
defun
random-form
(operators)
(append (list (random-elt operators))
(
loop
repeat 2
;
arity
collect (
let
((random-nr (random 100)))
(
cond
((< random-nr 50) (random-form operators))
((< random-nr 75) (random 10.0))
(t                '=input=))))))
The function works as follows: it creates a list of three items.  The
first item is a random operator and the second and third items are the
arguments to that operator:
(operator argument-1 argument-2)
The arguments are either a random number between 0.0 and 10.0
(arbitrary limit), a variable called
=INPUT=
(more about this later)
or,
and this is important
, another list of three items.  For
example:
(* =INPUT= 2.345)
or
(+ 6.789 (- =INPUT= 0.123))
So the RANDOM-FORM function will call itself recursively if needed.
The (arbitrary) probabilities for the ARGUMENT-1 and ARGUMENT-2 are:
50% of the time another random form, 25% of the time a random number
and 25% of the time the
=INPUT=
variable.
